questions.title: Level-Order Fill
questions.description:
A breadth-first crawler walks the chart level by level: fill out with the level-order visit — top to bottom, left to right within a level. Use a std::queue (the harness includes <queue> for you); stack< recursion emulation is banned. The harness prints out space-separated. The harness builds the tree from line 1: n and line 2: n level-order values (-1 = missing node). The program scaffolding (includes, the TNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void level_order(TNode* root, std::vector<int>& out)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n level-order values (-1 = NULL).

Output Format:
One line with the level-order sequence, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, the tree is non-empty

questions.description:
A mirroring check verifies the chart is symmetric: return 1 when the tree is a mirror image of itself — the left subtree mirrors the right subtree recursively (equal values at mirrored positions) — else 0. Pure pointer recursion with a mirrored pair helper; queue<, stack< and vector< are banned. The harness builds the tree from line 1: n and line 2: n level-order values (-1 = missing node). The program scaffolding (includes, the TNode struct and main) is already set up for you.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n level-order values (-1 = NULL).

Output Format:

Constraints:
